messages:
pagerbot: ALERT: High queue depth on gpu-hotqueue-3. autoscaler hit max_shards, token-throttles increasing, prefix-cache miss-rate spike detected. severity: SEV2

mike_sre: seeing the same in grafana. queue size ~ 86k reqs, 95th latency up 3x. also throttles on tiered API keys. Paging oncall. @tess_platform you up? :rotating_light:

mike_sre: runbook start: https://runbooks/internal/gpu-queue-surge - taking lead until cleared
\

tess_platform: oncall here, joining. quick snapshot: autoscaler logs show repeated "scale limit reached" for pool gpu-rt-prod, last scale event 00:02:14 UTC. any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Deploy notice: rolled out infra/autoscaler v2.7.3 -> v2.8.0 at 23:58 UTC (canary -> global). Change set included continuous-batcher tuning: batch_window_ms: 8 -> 60 and kv-prefix-ttl: 600 -> 120.

sam_ml: oh that change to batch_window_ms will blow up throughput for our request mix. it increases aggregation time and reduces throughput per GPU under hot short-queries. also ttl drop could cause prefix cache misses.

mike_sre: grabbing autoscaler status now: ```
infractl autoscaler status --pool gpu-rt-prod
POOL: gpu-rt-prod
current_shards: 48
max_shards: 48
queue_depth: 86234
scale_events: [throttled at 23:59, attempted +4 at 00:01 -> max]
last_scaled_by: policy-hot-queue
```

jin_ops: looking at runtime metrics: continuous_batching.active_batches dropped 40%, token/sec per GPU down 35%, prefix_cache.hit_rate dropped from 0.92 -> 0.37 after 23:58 deploy. that's consistent with both param changes.

mike_sre: impact estimate: sustained queue means degraded latency for hosted customers, token throttles for lower tiers. initial customer reports: 12 accounts reduced throughput, 3 reported errors. enterprise-cust-42 saw ~15% error spike.

kirti_support: logged alerts into zendesk. notifying CS and account teams for enterprise-cust-42. drafting customer message: "We are investigating increased latencies and throttles; mitigation underway."

mike_sre: mitigation plan (short): 1) increase max_shards temporary 2) rollback autoscaler roll 3) revert continuous batching param 4) bump prefix cache TTL back 5) protective rate-limits for lower tiers 6) monitor. executing now.

tess_platform: executing step 1: ```infractl autoscaler update --pool gpu-rt-prod --max-shards 64``` -> running. request accepted, provisioning spare nodes (best-effort).

sam_ml: I'm preparing rollback patch for autoscaler config. rolling canary rollback to v2.7.3.```deploy rollback infra/autoscaler v2.7.3 --strategy immediate```

deploy-bot: Rollback started at 00:10 UTC, status: canary reverted, global rollback queued.

mike_sre: step 3/4: reverting continuous batching and prefix ttl to safe defaults. applying: ```kubectl patch configmap runtime-batching -p '{"data":{"batch_window_ms":"8","kv_prefix_ttl_s":"600"}}'```

jin_ops: patched. observed prefix_cache.hit_rate climbing: 0.37 -> 0.68 in 30s. continuous_batching.active_batches recovering.

tess_platform: autoscaler max_shards update succeeded, new shards coming up. queue depth trending down: 86k -> 21k in 7 minutes. token throttles still present but declining.

mike_sre: added emergency rate-limit rule to protect capacity: ```policyctl apply rate-limit --scope public-tier --rps 1.5x baseline``` applied. helps cut noise.

kirti_support: customer update sent to affected list, CS monitoring responses. enterprise-cust-42 assigned SE for live assist.

sam_ml: confirming reverted deployment completed: deploy-bot shows rollback finished at 00:16 UTC and autoscaler v2.7.3 active everywhere.

mike_sre: final numbers at 00:22 UTC: queue_depth 3.1k, prefix_cache.hit_rate 0.85, token/sec per GPU near baseline. throttles dropped to normal.

tess_platform: moving to postmortem and RCA. immediate root cause: autoscaler rollout introduced continuous-batching change (batch_window_ms increased) and prefix cache TTL reduction; together they reduced effective throughput and increased cache miss amplification which caused demand to outstrip configured max_shards. autoscaler then hit its configured cap rather than autoscaling further.

mike_sre: action items: - revert to safe batching + ttl permanently until we have a validated workload matrix (owner: sam_ml, due: 48h) - add autoscaler canary guard to prevent simultaneous param changes that reduce throughput (owner: tess_platform, due: 72h) - increase temporary shard headroom for hot queues and automate emergency headroom policy (owner: jin_ops, due: 24h) - customer comms postmortem (owner: kirti_support, due: 48h)

kirti_support: noted. I'll coordinate timeline for affected customers.

mike_sre: handing off to incident lead for write-up. oncall cleared at 00:30 UTC. pagerbot: close incident when no further regressions detected for 2h.

pagerbot: RESOLVED: gpu-hotqueue-3 surge mitigated, autoscaler rollback complete. incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes.
